name: SharpHound / BloodHound
summary: Active Directory attack-path mapping. SharpHound is the collector; BloodHound ingests the data into a graph so operators can find shortest paths to Domain Admin and other high-value targets.
description: BloodHound uses graph theory to reveal hidden and unintended relationships in an Active Directory (and Azure AD/Entra) environment. SharpHound (C#) collects sessions, ACLs, group memberships, trusts, GPOs and more; the BloodHound UI then computes attack paths (e.g. 'who can reach Domain Admin'). Both attackers and defenders (and the Community Edition / legacy versions) use it.
usage: # import the resulting zip into the BloodHound GUI and run built-in queries
detection: High-volume LDAP queries enumerating users/groups/ACLs from a single host.
SAMR / network session enumeration (SharpHound Session/LoggedOn) across many hosts.
4662 with broad property reads; ldap traffic anomalies; honeytoken objects.
